text:
alisa: quick thread — observed weirdness with eviction signals across nodes when a tenant spikes. some nodes mark prefixes for immediate hard-evict while others emit soft-evict leases, and we end up with read-after-evict flaps. want to standardize a minimal cross-node "evict-candidate" signal we can use for coordination.

jamal: can you paste an example payload? trying to picture how many fields we'd need.

alisa: sketch:```
{
  "prefix_id": "tenant:123:prefA",
  "reason": "memory_pressure",
  "hotness_score": 0.78,        // 0..1 float
  "last_access_ts": 1798765400, // epoch
  "mode": "candidate"          // candidate | confirmed | cancel
}
```this would be lightweight, sent to shard-peers and indexed in local eviction window. if a peer sees multiple candidates for same prefix it can escalate to "confirmed" or defer based on local QoS.

maria: I like minimal fields. +1 to including last_access_ts so we can avoid demoting recently warmed prefixes. question: how do we avoid extra RPC chatter at scale?

henry: concern: if every node broadcasts candidates we'll overload the mesh. options: 1) piggyback on existing heartbeat/lease-fanout and include an aggregated "top-k eviction candidates" per beat, or 2) use a small gossip ring to diffuse signals. piggyback seems simplest.

jamal: piggyback makes sense. what about correctness when two nodes simultaneously confirm different actions (one confirms evict, other confirms retain)? we need deterministic tie-breaks so we don't flip-flop.

alisa: proposal: deterministic tie-breaker = (node_id, epoch) lexicographic AND we keep a short hysteresis window (configurable, default 2s) during which confirmed->hard-evict is delayed to let other nodes' beats arrive. also persist last_confirmed_action in ephemeral in-memory index to avoid double-apply.

maria: i'd add a safety fallback: if a node is about to hard-evict but local SLOs indicate high read rate, downgrade to soft-evict and schedule re-eval. basically conservative by default.

henry: engineering tradeoff: more conservative = fewer incorrect evicts but higher steady-state memory. we should expose a tenant-level policy: "aggressive" vs "conservative" to let platform teams pick.

jamal: test plan: 1) unit tests for tie-breaker ordering 2) microbench with synthetic hotset across 100 nodes to measure heartbeat payload growth and false-confirm rate 3) chaos test with partitions to ensure recovery. who wants the spike?

alisa: i'll do the spike for piggyback approach. will instrument: evict-candidate counter, confirmed-count, delayed-evict-timer, and cross-node disagreements metric.

ops-bot: <alert>Rolling sampling job noted 12k candidate signals/min during a tenant replay yesterday — filing incident-ops ticket #INC-2026-42</alert>

maria: nice — when you have the spike results can you include a short perf vs memory curve? that will help product decide default policy.

alisa: will do. quick open question: should the candidate payload include a small signature/hash of prefix contents (e.g., bloom hash) for cheap cross-checks before confirm? pros: cheaper validation, cons: adds compute and risk of false-negatives. thoughts?

henry: meh — prefer not to until we see real false-confirm cases. keep it simple v1. we can always add an optional field later.

jamal: agreed. +1 to incremental. thanks alisa — this sounds actionable. :thumbsup:

alisa: thanks — I'll post a short RFC follow-up with the spike plan and a proposed proto for the heartbeat payload.
